Cross-check (report only): company x tier x cycle totals from the payload join equal the workbook cycle sheets exactly for 7 industries; crypto differs only by the 4 company labels above.
Credit Union workbook had an Excel lock file (~$...) present, i.e. it was open in Excel; the on-disk bytes were read and were unchanged (sha256 and mtime) across the read.
Numbers are written with repr() (same serializer override as the study's build_workbooks.py) so real values round-trip exactly; the verifier recomputes nominal x multiplier as an exact double.

The negative control's extra failure 'real == nominal x CPI multiplier (697 rows)' is caused by openpyxl's default '%.16g' serializer used to save the tampered copy, not by a tamper; it shows the exact-double check has teeth.
